competitive_landscape: Today: a single daily BatamFast/Desaru ferry plus the congested road via the Causeway. No premium, on-demand, or clean option exists — the corridor is wide open and the road pain is the opening. Competitor presence is minimal, signalling unmet demand rather than a contested market.

journeys.today: ~90-min ferry running barely once a day, or a 2–2.5 h drive via Tuas and the Causeway jams.
journeys.with_navier: A direct ~45-min foiling crossing, booked in-app — no border queue.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Tanah Merah ↔ Desaru sits ~28 nm across the strait — comfortably inside the Pioneer II 70 nm all-electric envelope, multi-rotation on a charge.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required for the crossing; Quanta-LR extends onward up Johor's east coast to Tioman if the network grows.

grab.note: The under-served Malaysia crossing — more road-pain and arguably more traffic than the Riau crossing. A flagship cross-border GrabWater corridor.

regulatory_note: Cross-border Singapore↔Malaysia service touches both MPA (Singapore) clean-harbour-craft rules and Malaysian maritime/immigration at Desaru's CIQ ferry terminal — a defined, existing checkpoint.
seasonality: Desaru faces the South China Sea; the NE monsoon (Nov–Mar) brings stronger swell on the open east coast. Foils ride above the chop, extending the operable window beyond conventional fast-boats; sheltered routing into the resort jetties helps in peak monsoon.

signature_routes.label: Singapore East Coast ↔ Desaru resort jetties

summary: Desaru Coast is Johor's flagship beach-resort destination (Westin, Hard Rock, One&Only, Anantara, the Els Club) sitting just across the strait from Singapore. Today it is served by a single daily ferry or a 2–2.5 hour drive through Tuas and Causeway congestion — a glaring gap for a destination this close and this premium.
tagline: Singapore's nearest resort coast — yet barely reachable by sea.

use_cases.body: Tanah Merah ↔ Desaru (~28 nm) is within all-electric range. An in-app foiling crossing turns a once-a-day ferry or a Causeway slog into a fast, smooth ~45-minute hop — the most road-painful, least sea-served crossing from Singapore.
